question: A 39-year-old man presents with painless swelling of the right testes and a sensation of heaviness. The physical examination revealed an intra-testicular solid mass that could not be felt separately from the testis. After a thorough evaluation, he was diagnosed with testicular seminoma. Which of the following group of lymph nodes are most likely involved?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Testicular seminoma -> metastasis -> lymphatic spread -> Para-aortic lymph nodes -> 95% CHAIN: Testicular seminoma -> lymphatic drainage pattern -> Para-aortic lymph nodes -> 90% CHAIN: Testicular seminoma -> lymphatic involvement -> Para-aortic lymph nodes -> 95%
enhanced_information: Testicular seminoma commonly metastasizes to the para-aortic lymph nodes. The lymphatic drainage pattern of testicular seminoma supports the involvement of para-aortic lymph nodes. Evidence paths confirm the connection between lymphatic vessels and the para-aortic nodes, strengthening the likelihood of para-aortic lymph node involvement in this case.
analysis: Testicular seminoma commonly metastasizes to the para-aortic lymph nodes based on standard medical knowledge and the enhanced information provided. The lymphatic drainage pattern supports this involvement, and the evidence paths confirm the connection between lymphatic vessels and the para-aortic nodes. Therefore, the most likely correct option is the para-aortic lymph nodes.
